findings.subject: BOOSTER subtype counts
findings.finding: Abstract reports cryo13/thermal31; Figure3 caption and Discussion report13/29 among42 analysed. Main text says ablation modality was selected by oncologist, not randomised. Preserve the discrepancy, do not silently adopt31 or rank procedures.

findings.subject: Radiopharmaceutical guidance scope
findings.finding: FDA129547 is August2019 nonclinical studies and labeling guidance. Animal biodistribution and dosimetry can inform human study design; this does not establish a universal clinical schedule or therapeutic dose from one tracer scan.

findings.subject: oligoprogression
findings.finding: Current tldr instructs treat the spots and keep the pill, and definition restricts to one/two lesions on targeted therapy. CURB uses up to5 progressive sites after systemic treatment and different cohort outcomes. Replace blanket instruction with bounded definition and study evidence.

findings.subject: biologically-effective-dose
findings.finding: Current tldr says any schedule; summary implies general interchangeability of external beam, brachytherapy and reirradiation. Qualify the basic equal-fraction model, repair/time assumptions and clinical limits.

findings.subject: linear-quadratic-model
findings.finding: Current summary gives unbounded low/high ratio and model-breakdown claims. Qualify model extrapolation and tissue/endpoint assumptions; preserve any untouched RBE clause as earlier text not re-verified by this cohort.

findings.subject: cell-composition-confound
findings.finding: Current summary says any whole-sample or spatial-region measurement averages the mixture and presents deconvolution/purity as usual corrections. Distinguish aggregate RNA from cell fractions/density and model-based estimates from direct counts.

findings.subject: Clinical comparison uncertainty
findings.finding: NRG-BR002 did not meet the phaseII go/no-go signal; the PFS95%CI0.57to1.47 does not prove zero effect. CURB prespecified cancer cohorts differ. BOOSTER primary clock begins before randomisation; secondary randomisation-clock analyses are separately reported, not grounds to declare its randomised comparison automatically biased.

findings.subject: Conventional CD8 recognition
findings.finding: Keep peptide-classI HLA recognition scoped to conventional alpha-beta CD8 T cells. Prior published immune cohort carries the supporting scoped fields; no all-T-cell universal claim is accepted.

findings.subject: PACIFIC correction
findings.finding: Crossref and EuropePMC resolve DOI10.1200/JCO.22.01023, PMID35671538. Direct publisher returned403. Search-extracted publisher text mentions a cisplatin forest-plot count and a prior TTDM cutoff date; that remains a lead until raw notice text is obtained. Do not claim notice fully read from registry metadata.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: Surgery is local therapy too, and in early breast cancer it is the most common one. This guide focuses on ablation and radiation, so read [breast surgery basics](/wiki/education/concepts/therapeutics/local-therapies/breast-surgery-basics), [completion surgery](/wiki/education/concepts/therapeutics/local-therapies/completion-surgery) and [regional nodal irradiation after neoadjuvant therapy](/wiki/education/concepts/therapeutics/local-therapies/regional-nodal-irradiation-after-neoadjuvant-therapy) for the operation and the radiation questions that follow it.

retainedSourceOpen.semanticAssessment: Surgery as local therapy is carried, but the comparative most-common ranking in early breast cancer is not established by the raw NCI surgery page. Most breast-cancer/DCIS patients having surgery does not prove a ranking among local modalities.
residualClauses: The source sentence ranks surgery as the most common local therapy in early breast cancer; no read source establishes that comparative frequency.
